{
"Domain-Driven Design": "A software development approach that centers the design of code and architecture around a deep understanding of the business domain, using shared models and language between developers and domain experts.",
"Business Domain": "The specific sphere of knowledge, activity, or problem space that a software system is built to support, encompassing the rules, processes, and concepts of the business it serves.",
"Bounded Context": "An explicit boundary within which a particular domain model is defined, consistent, and applicable, isolating it from other contexts that may use different models or terminology.",
"Model": "A conceptual abstraction that represents selected aspects of a domain, capturing its entities, relationships, and behaviors in a form useful for solving business problems.",
"Entity": "A domain object defined primarily by a unique identity that persists over time, rather than by its attributes, allowing it to be tracked through changes in state.",
"Identity": "The distinguishing characteristic that uniquely identifies an entity across its lifecycle, remaining constant even as the entity's attributes change.",
"Lifecycle": "The sequence of states and transitions an entity passes through from its creation to its eventual archival or deletion within the domain.",
"Value Object": "A domain object that is defined solely by its attributes, has no distinct identity, and is treated as interchangeable when its values are equal.",
"Immutability": "A property of an object whereby its state cannot be modified after creation, ensuring consistency and enabling safe sharing across the system.",
"Attribute": "A named property or characteristic of a domain object that describes some aspect of its state or value.",
"Aggregate": "A cluster of related domain objects treated as a single unit for the purposes of data changes and consistency, with access controlled through a single root entity.",
"Aggregate Root": "The single entity within an aggregate that serves as the entry point for external access and enforces the invariants and consistency rules of the aggregate as a whole.",
"Repository": "An abstraction that provides collection-like access to aggregates, encapsulating the logic required to retrieve and store them while hiding persistence details from the domain layer.",
"Persistence": "The mechanism by which domain objects are stored in and retrieved from a durable medium, allowing their state to survive beyond the execution of a program.",
"Ubiquitous Language": "A shared, rigorous vocabulary developed collaboratively by developers and domain experts, used consistently in code, documentation, and conversation within a bounded context.",
"Terminology": "The specific set of terms and their agreed-upon meanings used to describe concepts within a domain, forming the vocabulary that underpins clear communication."
}
